statements.text: The Prime Minister says the UK's assessment is that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He says the UK will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC.
The Prime Minister welcomes Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. He says Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.
The government has announced new funding to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that covers over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity.

Ahead of President Zelenskyy's visit, the Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military aid and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and to accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which it says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. It has committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million missile package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter requirements.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said he urges partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, as the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin. He is pressing this at the IMF meetings in Bangkok.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster in its support. He said Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy to Downing Street. The leaders reflected on their call and on Russia's attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure since Trump called for an energy ceasefire, and underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles.

The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for use in Ukraine, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners. He said the UK would also continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, which the Prime Minister says would add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, emissions trading progress, linking energy systems, a new youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration.

The Prime Minister says he believes the UK's chances at the summit will be enhanced by being open to discussing the relationship with the EU in the longer term. He says the immediate priority is a successful summit outcome, after which a serious dialogue about long-term options should be set up.

The Prime Minister will call on the Scottish Government to work with the UK Government through No10 North and the Scotland Office to develop a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland, and says he wants to design that model together in the months ahead.

The Prime Minister offers Scotland a model of localised employment support, similar to England's but shaped by Holyrood. The National Economic Council is to meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First Minister and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland, for the first time since he became Prime Minister, to put the offer on the table.

Douglas Alexander said power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament. He called the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government a genuine one, and said the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

Britain has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refuelling support. The Prime Minister confirms a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions, and condemns the attacks on King Khalid International Airport.
The Prime Minister says the UK will meet its NATO commitments in full. He says that in Berlin he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership to tackle Russia's hybrid threats.
The Prime Minister confirmed in New York that the UK will place AI centre stage in its G20 presidency in 2027, capturing its opportunities while guarding against its risks.
The Scottish Government has agreed this week to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west.

The Great British Railways headquarters will be at Becketwell, a brownfield site in Derby city centre. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, and the site will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff, with an estimated £151 million boost to the Derby economy.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway. She said she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home, bringing jobs, investment and opportunity to Derby.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship. Pat McFadden said this is part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
